newsitem.title: USA: CME plans half-tick price change for some Eurodlrs.
newsitem.headline: CME plans half-tick price change for some Eurodlrs.

text.p: The Chicago Mercantile Exchange plans to introduce half-tick price increments for spot-month Eurodollar futures and futures-options, according to a bulletin from Wednesday's CME board meeting.

Under a plan approved by the CME board, half-tick trading would begin on the first business day of the spot month for the spot-month contract and continue through the last trading day of that contract.
The board devised the plan, which requires regulatory approval, "for the purpose of maintaining the competitiveness of the exchange's interest rate complex," the bulletin said.
The plan would cut the tick size, or smallest price change, for the spot Eurodollar contracts during the delivery month to 0.005, worth $12.50 each.
Currently each tick in Eurodollar futures is 0.01, worth $25.00.
The proposed changes also apply to the exchanges's LIBOR futures and options.

The CME board also said it plans to move serial-month Eurodollar futures into the LIBOR trading pit, beginning with the January 1997 contract which will be listed for trading on October 15. -Derivatives Desk 312-408-8750 E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
